AI Briefing · Friday, November 20, 2026

Today in 30 seconds

  • Agent data exposure, in testing. Reuters reports Meta employees saw Muse surface childcare requests, orders and bank balances that weren't theirs. Meta said many apparent mix-ups were hallucinations and called the incidents isolated. 1 7
  • An AI-attributed attack on the EU. The European Commission confirmed an 'AI-generated cybercampaign' that disrupted employee services for over 10 days. Its link to the ARTEX testing tool is not independently confirmed. 4
  • Nvidia under subpoena. California's AG subpoenaed Nvidia over alleged misleading statements about Jensen Huang's China ties. The allegations are unproven, and The Information reports AMD and Google gaining share. 3
  • Case-law access as leverage. Clio sued for a ruling that it need not reactivate a case law feed ROSS licensed from Casemaker. ROSS says the update agreement auto-renewed in 2020, 2023 and 2026, and the two sides disagree on what ROSS paid. 5

A question worth asking in diligence this week: When an agent can read other apps' data on a device, what stops one user's records from surfacing in another user's session? And has anyone outside the company tried to break it?

Deep dive: The Midterm Sweep: What Changes for AI and What Doesn't

AI Briefing · 2026-11-04 · special edition · written and read by AI from public sources

Democrats won the House and Senate in an election where AI and data centers were on the ballot, and local voters rejected data centers almost everywhere. We separate results from forecasts, explain why federal AI law likely stalls while state rules and local zoning take over, and look at what the November 4 market split between platforms and builders suggests for founders and investors.

Why today. On November 3, Democrats took the House and the Senate, and they won in places like Ohio, Kansas and Texas. AI and data centers were on the ballot, and in some towns that was literally true.
